minutes.headline: Committee lifted the hiring freeze for two jobs and ratified two union agreements; heard a student mental-health screening report.
minutes.summary: The remote meeting opened with the superintendent evaluation process, then a presentation on universal mental health screening at the high school. The committee then voted on a line transfer, the Dragon playground refurbishment, an Ace program tuition-in proposal, a limited lifting of the hiring freeze, two union memoranda, the collaborative agreement, a donation and the quarterly report. The superintendent reported on federal relief funds and reopening plans, and the FinCom report flagged state-aid uncertainty.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to temporarily lift the hiring freeze so listed positions can be posted, with a disclaimer allowing stipends to be prorated.
It ratified two union memoranda 5-0: one with the LEA on the master teacher program, one with the secretaries and clerks on vacation carryover.
It approved the Ace Program proposal to allow tuition-in students 5-0; contracts will go to legal only when a student is interested.
The committee heard a presentation on universal mental health screening; the superintendent agreed to send parents a standalone notice on the counseling consent form.
It also approved a small line transfer, the Dragon playground refurbishment, the Keystone collaborative agreement and a donation, and accepted the FY20 quarterly report, all 5-0.

why_it_matters: The hiring freeze lift and the secretaries' vacation carryover touch the school payroll, and the business manager said the carryover may have a cost that was not quantified.
State aid for next year is uncertain, so the FY20 year-end moves and any cut in state aid could affect the school budget the town is asked to fund, mostly through taxes.
Ace tuition-in students could bring in tuition that offsets program costs, but the rates have not been set.
watch_next: The superintendent evaluation using the new draft rubric is due for presentation at the June 17th meeting, with member feedback going to the chair first.
Ace tuition-in rates are still to be set by the business manager, the committee and the superintendent.
